title: Report a partially-applied VCF Automation change accurately
prompt:
Our platform team runs VMware Cloud Foundation 9.1 and drives VCF Automation - the 9.1 successor to vRealize Automation and Aria Automation - from PowerShell. VCF PowerCLI 9.1 (`VCF.PowerCLI`) is installed on every runner and we never vendor any part of it into our own repositories.

This working directory holds our `VcfAutomation.Change` module. Start with `README.md`, then `docs/contract.json`: VCF Automation publishes no API specification, so that contract was transcribed by hand from the xAPIs reference guides on developer.broadcom.com, and `docs/official_sources.json` records every page that was read, the operation it documents and the date. The contract lists the only five operations this module may call, the documented query parameters for each, and the body fields of the two write operations.

Already written, and working: the HTTP layer (`Private/Invoke-VcfaRequest.ps1`, which deliberately returns error statuses instead of raising them), the SDDC Manager token path that goes through `VMware.Sdk.Vcf.SddcManager`, and `Connect-VcfaOrgSession`. Three functions are stubs that throw:

  * `Initialize-VcfaCatalogItemRequest`   - builds the CatalogItemRequest body
  * `Initialize-VcfaResourceActionRequest` - builds the ResourceActionRequest body
  * `Invoke-VcfaCatalogItemChange`         - runs the change and reports on it

Implement them. The change is five steps: resolve the project by name, resolve the catalog item by name, request the catalog item into that project, find the named resource in the deployment that comes back, then submit a day-2 action against that resource.

Three things have gone wrong with this flow before, and all three need to be handled.

First, and most important: a change that gets partway through must be reported as what it actually was. Last month a resize was rejected because the deployment was still provisioning - the appliance answered the day-2 action with 409, our script threw, and the log said only that the change had failed. Nobody realised a deployment had already been created; it sat unowned for two days before anyone found it. So `Invoke-VcfaCatalogItemChange` must not throw because a step failed. It returns a report that says which steps succeeded, which step failed and why (status code, plus whatever message the appliance returned), and which steps were consequently never attempted - and it keeps the deployment id and name on the result even when a later step fails, because that identifier is the only handle an operator has. Do not try to tidy up after a failure; deleting or patching the deployment is outside the contract.

Second: request bodies that send empty values. Every field in both write bodies is optional, so "the caller did not supply this" is the only signal the service gets. A field the caller left unset must be absent from the JSON - not `null`, not `""`, not `0`. A field the caller did supply must be sent, with the right JSON type. This is what the `Initialize-*` builders are for, and it is the same convention the generated `VMware.Sdk.Vcf.*` body builders follow.

Third: calls that drift off the contract. Only those five operations, and for each one only the query parameters `docs/contract.json` lists for it. Where a filter you want has no documented parameter, filter client-side.

The docstrings on the three stubs pin down the exact step names, report properties and step statuses expected, so read them before you start.

Check your work with:

    pwsh -NoLogo -NoProfile -File tests/Verify-Change.ps1

That drives the module against `mock/Start-VcfaMock.ps1`, a loopback test double that reads `docs/contract.json` and serves only the operations it names, logging every request it receives. No appliance is involved and nothing outside 127.0.0.1 is contacted. Leave `tests/`, `mock/`, `docs/contract.json` and `docs/official_sources.json` alone - implement the change flow, not the harness.

workspace.note: The contents of files/ are the working directory the task starts from.

prerequisites.description: VCF PowerCLI 9.1, the environment's PowerShell SDK for VMware Cloud Foundation. Provides VMware.Sdk.Vcf.SddcManager, which the module's shipped bearer-token path calls. Installed by the environment; never vendored into the workspace.
prerequisites.requiredForVerificationNote: Verification exercises the change flow with an already-issued token via Connect-VcfaOrgSession -AccessToken, so it does not import the SDK and does not depend on this install having succeeded.

verification.successCriteria: Exit code 0. The script prints one line per assertion and a PASS/FAIL summary; every assertion must pass.
verification.network: None. The test double binds 127.0.0.1 only and no VMware endpoint is contacted.
verification.dependencies: PowerShell 7.2 or later. No Pester, no PowerCLI, no other modules.
whatIsChecked: The five requests reach the appliance in contract order, each matching a contract operation, each carrying the bearer token.

No request falls outside the contract and no request carries a query parameter the contract does not document for that operation - in particular the project lookup must not invent a name filter, because none is documented.
The catalog lookup scopes to the resolved project id and confirms the exact item name client-side, since 'search' is a substring match and the double returns a retired near-match first.
Both write bodies contain exactly the fields the caller supplied: unset optional fields are absent rather than null or empty, supplied ones are present with the right JSON type.

The day-2 action is rejected with 409, the function returns instead of throwing, and the report marks the first four steps succeeded and the fifth failed with the status code and the appliance's message.
The report still carries the deployment id and name created before the failure, and the resolved project, catalog item and resource ids.
Project lookup follows pagination when the service returns more than one page, without inventing a name query parameter.
When the first step fails instead, only project-list requests are made, nothing is created, the four later steps are reported as skipped, and no identifiers are claimed.
A fully successful change returns Status Succeeded, no FailedStep and five succeeded step records.

referenceFix.note: Implements only the three stubs. Verification exits 1 before the patch and 0 after it.
